topic: Policy target feasibility test over a scenario set
idea: HCMC set targets (public transport share 22-26% by 2015, 47-50% by 2020) and six scenarios were simulated (business as usual; rail 2015; plus parking fee +100% in inner districts; parking places -20%; -40%; plus BRT) to test whether the target is reachable: best case 24.5% (18% rail, 6.5% bus) so the target is infeasible. Output also CO2 by scenario (BAU +30%, best case flat).
does: Given a target for a KPI (bus share, mean speed, car share) and a set of lever scenarios, run them and report the best achievable value, the gap to the target, and which lever contributed most; says plainly 'not reachable with these levers'.
inputs: target KPI and value, list of lever scenarios
outputs: achieved value per scenario, gap, lever ranking
existing: partial: run_experiment (scenarios vs baseline), choose_modes, institution_mode_split
cite: Ho Chi Minh City, MARS modelling exercise, Fig 5-6
notes: Levers on mode share (parking fee, parking supply) need a cost term in mode choice; ACMS has institution mode split with cost.

idea: In the system-dynamics model, congested motorised speeds fall while bicycle speed stays constant (model assumption), so cyclists gain a relative travel-speed advantage and the bicycle mode share rises in the BAU run; mode shares respond to simulated speed in every period.
does: Iterate choose_modes with link times from the previous run until mode shares and speeds are consistent (fixed point), instead of one pass on free flow or one run.
outputs: equilibrium mode shares and travel times
existing: partial: choose_modes (times from free flow or one run), assign_routes (successive averages)
cite: Ho Chi Minh City MARS results
notes: ACMS not_built notes choose_modes uses free flow or one run; this is the feedback.

topic: Flood-prone roads as capacity reduction with relative comparison
idea: Flood impact: roads are rarely fully blocked, only capacity-reduced for a few hours; model it by severity and location, compare a calibrated base-case model with an analysis-case model (relative difference, because absolute effects are uncertain); indicators: cut-off of crucial civic infrastructure, affected sensitive areas, shops, offices, vendors, pedestrians; plus travel time and emissions.
does: Scenario: chosen roads get a capacity (speed and lane) factor for a time window, run paired against baseline, and report delay plus which institutions (hospital, school) lose reachability inside a time threshold.
inputs: roads, capacity factor, window, severity, institutions
outputs: delay change, institutions cut off or with reach drop
existing: partial: critical_links (static closure, extra vehicle-hours and demand cut off), schedule_emergency
notes: Same mechanism as the work-zone and incident idea (timed capacity reduction on a road).

topic: Bus priority options compared by bus speed and fleet hours
idea: Corridor case study: option 1 (queue-jump lane with pre-signal, signal optimisation, stop reorganisation, parallel para-transit removed, accepted capacity loss for cars) raised average bus speed 18 to 23 km/h and cut bus operating hours 219,912 to 177,140 bus-h/yr (about 20 percent less for identical supply); option 2 (widened road, median bus lane, bigger vehicles) reached 26 km/h at 147,465 bus-h/yr; fuel per year -365 t and -885 t.
does: Report per bus line the average bus speed, round-trip time, operating hours per day and the fleet needed for a headway (round trip / headway), so TSP, bus lanes and signal changes are compared in fleet cost as well as delay.
outputs: bus speed, round trip, fleet size needed, bus-hours/yr
existing: partial: results by vehicle type, TSP passenger delay and wait per trip
notes: A dedicated bus lane and queue-jump with pre-signal are not options in ACMS (TSP agent only); would need a bus-lane lane-use restriction.

topic: Per-link emissions from volumes by traffic situation
idea: TEMT method: for each road link assign an average-speed category (from volume-delay functions), classify its HBEFA traffic situation (road type and speed range, optionally level of service), take the emission factor for each vehicle class weighted by the local fleet (emission standard, engine size, fuel), and multiply the daily volume of each class by the weighted factor to give kg per km per day per link (CH4, CO, CO2, HC, NOx, N2O, NH3, PM, SO2); results mapped on the network.
does: Light emission accounting without acceleration data: per link, vehicles by type x emission factor looked up by mean speed band and road type, giving kg per km per day, a network total and a map layer, so scenarios can be compared on CO2, NOx and PM.
inputs: run (link flows by type and mean speeds), emission factor table by vehicle type and speed band (user supplied)
outputs: emissions per link and total by pollutant, map overlay
cite: Gauteng, TEMT Transport Emission Model, Fig 3
notes: HBEFA factors are not in the source; a small default table (CO2 g/km vs speed) would have to be supplied. Also covers the emissions KPI gap noted from AgentSUMO and ChatSUMO.

idea: Scenario analysis 2007-2040 over uncertain parameters (oil price, population growth); a 'robust measure' is one that appears in most scenarios independent of the uncertain parameters; BAU baseline plus policies likely to be implemented.
does: After an experiment run under several demand levels or conditions, flag the design changes whose benefit has the same sign and is significant in all (or most) conditions, versus those that only win under one.
inputs: experiment results across demand scales or conditions
outputs: per measure: share of conditions where it wins, worst-case difference
cite: Gauteng Implementation and Outlook; Outcomes, Models and Planning Tools

idea: Design criteria for a new town network: the next public-transport stop reachable within 300 m everywhere; minibus catchment under 250 m; high-capacity arteries, feeders, minibuses; BRT on separate lanes as first high-capacity option upgradable to light rail on the same lanes.
does: Share of people (institution catchments, homes) and of institutions within a walking distance of a bus stop (default 300 m, straight line or along roads), and the uncovered institutions listed with the nearest stop distance.
outputs: coverage share, uncovered list, map overlay
cite: Tehran-Karaj Hashtgerd, High-quality Public Transport Service
notes: Simple geometry in metres; fits the ACMS vector rule.

topic: Parking guarantee effect on mode share
idea: Surveyed car shares in five European cities (Besancon, Grenoble, Toulouse, Bern, Geneva) are far higher for destinations where parking is guaranteed than where it is not (the guaranteed-parking car share is above 90% in each); parking supply strongly drives car use. Concept of a reduced parking-lot factor, with the space a conventional parking factor of 1.0 consumes in a 35 ha pilot area.
does: Add a parking availability term to the institution mode choice: a car alternative whose utility drops when parking at the door is limited (spaces per employee), so TDM or parking-cap scenarios shift people to Walk and Bus.
inputs: institution parking spaces per person, penalty coefficient
existing: partial: institution_mode_split (cost per km term, constants)
notes: The table in the extracted text is garbled, so only the direction and rough size of the effect are recorded.

topic: Induced travel from a constant travel-time budget
idea: Travel time budgets are about constant (0.85 to 1.7 hours across cities); extra network speed is spent on longer trips, so capacity or speed gains raise distances and resource use rather than saving time.
does: Warn when a design makes trips faster that part of the saved time will return as longer trips or more trips; optionally apply a demand elasticity to travel time in scenario demand.
outputs: demand uplift and net delay change
notes: No elasticity value given; user supplies one.
